newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES RISE IN LETHARGIC TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES RISE IN LETHARGIC TRADE.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures ended higher across the board in lethargic trade on Thursday.
But traders said the metal's rally in London overnight for the most part failed to attract individual investors from the volatile precious metals market.

"The Tokyo market is also looking upwards," said a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses. "But people are looking at precious metals." The June contract gained 0.3 yen to 202.1 yen per kg and the April added 1.7 yen to 205.7 yen. Others posted gains of between 1.5 and 2.4 yen. The estimated volume was 1,590 lots.

On the Tokyo precious metals market, some contracts, mainly platinum, fell by their daily limits in the latest swings against the backdrop of a tight physical market despite the resumption of Russian exports.
In London overnight, three months aluminium clawed up $20.50 to $1,741.50, heading back towards their recent high.
